page: Microsoft Azure D128ds_v7 is an enterprise-scale general-purpose virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processors on the x86_64 architecture, providing 64 physical cores and 128 execution threads with clock frequencies reaching 4.2 GHz. CPU resources are backed by 480 MB of shared L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware support for Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector pipelines. The hardware footprint includes 512 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 4 GB per vCPU distribution, and 7,560 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage. Discrete GPUs are absent from this configuration.

Empirical benchmark evaluations confirm the strength of the system in highly parallel operations. The instance records top-tier multi-core performance in stress-ng and PassMark CPU suites, complemented by cached memory read bandwidth exceeding 10,000 GB/sec and sustained uncached read throughput of 658.72 GB/sec. Database operations and in-memory key-value processing achieve top-tier brackets, with Redis SET operations scaling to 204.83 million operations per second and static web throughput reaching 160.54 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core execution benchmarks sit within the median performance band, indicating that strictly serial workloads do not realize the efficiency gains seen in thread-parallel tasks. LLM prompt processing also demonstrates strong throughput via matrix acceleration, whereas token generation rates remain average without discrete GPU hardware.

Resource consolidation is the primary architectural advantage of the D128ds_v7. Packaging 128 vCPUs, 512 GB of memory, and extensive local NVMe disk into a single node minimizes multi-node networking overhead and optimizes compute density per host. This balance delivers efficient operational throughput for large relational databases, in-memory caching systems, distributed ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency enterprise web applications requiring rapid local scratch space.
description: Microsoft Azure D128ds_v7 is a high-capacity general-purpose virtual machine built on x86_64 architecture. Powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processors clocked up to 4.2 GHz across 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs, the system features a 480 MB L3 cache alongside advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions including AVX-512 and AMX. It pairs 512 GB of system memory with 7,560 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Benchmark measurements demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded processing, exceptional memory bandwidth, and outstanding throughput in Redis operations and static web serving. While single-core compute operates at average levels, its parallel throughput and large cache architecture provide strong resource density for dense computing. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators. Microsoft Azure D128ds_v7 is technically aligned with large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems, extensive multi-threaded batch compilation, and high-concurrency web serving tiers requiring low-latency NVMe scratch capacity.
